hints.title: Run-Length Segment Compression
hints.text: Group consecutive identical characters into contiguous blocks characterized by character and span length.

hints.title: Single Block Extension
hints.text: For a block of character c, if the total count of c across the entire string exceeds block length, we can borrow a matching character from elsewhere, reaching length plus 1.

hints.title: Bridge Across Unit Gap
hints.text: If block i and block i + 2 share the same character and are separated by a bridge of length 1, combine their lengths. If total frequency exceeds the sum, add 1 for an external swap.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def maxRepOpt1(self, text: str) -> int:
        counts = Counter(text)
        groups = []
        i = 0
        n = len(text)
        while i < n:
            j = i
            while j < n and text[j] == text[i]:
                j += 1
            groups.append((text[i], j - i))
            i = j
        
        res = 0
        for i, (ch, length) in enumerate(groups):
            # Case 1: single block with an external character swap
            res = max(res, min(length + 1, counts[ch]))
            # Case 2: two blocks separated by a single different character
            if i + 2 < len(groups) and groups[i + 2][0] == ch and groups[i + 1][1] == 1:
                combined = length + groups[i + 2][1]
                res = max(res, min(combined + 1, counts[ch]))
        return res
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all O(N^2) pairwise swaps takes quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Run-length encoding condenses the string into O(N) blocks, enabling local bridge evaluation in linear time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize both the single-block expansion case and the unit-gap bridge combination case.
complexity.notes: Total frequency cap prevents borrowing a non-existent extra character.
